IO3_transformations.algorithm: Query group_members table for (group_id, user_id). Fetch role.
Lookup role. Compare against permissions matrix. Return true/false.
Verify assigner has permission to assign (founder/admin only). Update group_members.role. Notify user.

DW1_upstream_pipeline.description: User joins group (via invite code, request, or auto-add). Default role: member (or follower if follower groups enabled).

DW2_downstream_pipeline.description: User's role looked up and permission checked against matrix
If permitted: execute action (send message, create channel, etc). If denied: show error.
If action taken: log to audit_log (especially for admin/mod actions)

P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: Permission checking latency (should be very fast, <50ms). Role assignment coordination (especially founder transfer). Permissions matrix complexity (many roles × many actions).
P.P2_defensibility: Explicit roles prevent unauthorized actions. Permissions matrix is simple and verifiable. Founder transfer is controlled operation (only founder can initiate). Audit log tracks all role changes.
P.P3_confidence_level: Very high confidence. Simple role-based access control (RBAC) is well-established pattern. Permissions matrix is deterministic.
P4_failure_modes: Permission check fails → action denied even though user has permission (mitigate: comprehensive test of permissions matrix)
Role assignment race condition → two people promoted simultaneously (mitigate: database constraint on founder, one-founder-per-group)
Founder transfer blocked → group stuck without admin (mitigate: super-admin override in system)
Permission escalation → user gains unauthorized permission (mitigate: audit all role changes)
P.P5_backup_plan: If permission check unavailable: deny action (fail-closed). If role assignment fails: retry with exponential backoff. If founder transfer fails: system admin can override.
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Simulate permission check failure. Test race condition on founder transfer. Test permission escalation attempts. Test edge cases: user has role, role gets deleted, user still has old permissions.
P.P7_testing_strategy: Unit tests for permissions matrix (test each role × action combination). Integration tests for role assignment. Load tests for permission checking (1000 checks/s). End-to-end tests for founder transfer workflow. Security audit for permission escalation possibilities.
P.P8_benchmarks: Permission check: <50ms. Role lookup: <100ms. Role assignment: <200ms. Founder transfer: <500ms. False positive (permission granted incorrectly): 0%. False negative (permission denied incorrectly): 0%.

L.L1_legal_considerations: Role-based access prevents unauthorized moderation/removal. Audit trail tracks who did what (accountability). Founder transfer is controlled (prevents hostile takeover). Follower role enables observation without participation (reduces liability).
L.L3_consent_requirements: Implicit consent to role rules by joining group. No separate consent needed.
L.L4_liability_notes: Moderation actions (member removal) must be auditable. Mitigation: all mod actions logged. Founder transfer must be transparent (both parties see change). Permission escalation could enable abuse. Mitigation: audit trail + regular review.

F.F1_cost_considerations: Role storage: <10B per member (just role enum). Permissions matrix: static (no cost). Permission checking: negligible compute.
F.F3_revenue_impact: Role system enables moderation (safe groups, higher engagement). Moderate positive impact.

S.S1_cybersecurity: Roles are stored plaintext (low sensitivity). Founder role has single-leader constraint (database-enforced). Permission checks cached (prevent oracle attacks on permission system). Rate limiting on role assignment (prevent spam promotion).
S.S2_data_privacy: Role list is semi-public (members see each other's roles). No sensitive data in roles.
S.S3_encryption_requirements: NR - no encryption needed (roles are not sensitive)
S.S4_access_control: Only founder/admin can assign roles. Users can view own role and group member roles. Public roles list visible to group members.
S.S5_audit_requirements: Log all role assignments and changes. Log all permission denials (for troubleshooting). Audit trail retention: 1 year.

X.X1_notes: Roles are essential for group governance. Five-level hierarchy (founder, admin, moderator, member, follower) balances flexibility with simplicity. Founder single-leader constraint prevents power struggles. Follower role unique to Beacon (enables observation without participation).
X2_open_questions: Can admin promote another admin? (yes, for delegation)
Can founder transfer to admin? (yes, with both parties confirming)
What if founder leaves group? (admin auto-inherits founder? or group orphaned?)
Can member see who has admin role? (yes, but not admin emails or sensitive info)
X.X3_related_research: Role-based access control (RBAC) patterns. Permission matrices in governance. Community moderation best practices.
